acip: CHOS THAMS CAD CES GZUGS NAS RNAM MKHYEN GYI BAR GYI CHOS THAMS CAD RANG GI CHA SHAS LA BRTEN NAS GRUB PAS NA THA SNYAD DU RGYU 'BRAS BSLU BA MED PA DANG , DGAG BYA RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DMIGS GTAD ZHIG NAS BDEN PAR GRUB PA'AM, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I DNGOS PO CUNG ZAD TZAM YANG MED PAR RTOGS PA DE RGYAL BA DGYES PA'I LAM YIN,
wylie: chos thams cad ces gzugs nas rnam mkhyen gyi bar gyi chos thams cad rang gi cha shas la brten nas grub pas na tha snyad du rgyu 'bras bslu ba med pa dang , dgag bya rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dmigs gtad zhig nas bden par grub pa'am, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i dngos po cung zad tsam yang med par rtogs pa de rgyal ba dgyes pa'i lam yin
english: The expression "all objects" refers to each and every object from basic physical matter on up to the omniscience of a Buddha. They all exist in dependence upon their parts, so in a manner of speaking their "cause and effect can never fail." The antithesis, which we seek to disprove, is that these objects could have the solid existence they appear to have: that they could exist naturally. "When they lose all solid appearance"--that is, when we perceive that there is not a single thing in the universe which has any true or natural existence--then we have found "the path that pleases the Buddhas."

acip: DE YANG NAM ZHIG RES 'JOG MED PA ZHES CHOS THAMS CAD LA MING RKYANG BTAGS YOD TZAM GYI DGE SDIG BYA BYED THAMS CAD 'THAD PA DANG , BTAGS DON BTZAL BA'I TSE NA CHOS DE DANG DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PA'I STONG PA GNYIS
wylie: de yang nam zhig res 'jog med pa zhes chos thams cad la ming rkyang btags yod tsam gyi dge sdig bya byed thams cad 'thad pa dang , btags don btsal ba'i tshe na chos de dang de rang bzhin gyis grub pa rdul tsam yang med pa'i stong pa gnyis
english: Now here's what we mean when we say that "at some point they no longer alternate." We take two things: first, the fact that everything about the way things work, and about good deeds and bad deeds, is perfectly proper, despite the fact that no single object is anything more than labels, just names. Secondly there is the fact that, when we try to seek out the thing that got the name, we find only emptiness: that there is not a single atom of natural existence in whatever object we have chosen.

acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, DNGOS PO RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR 'DOD PA'I PHYOGS LA, KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS MA BLANGS KYANG LAS 'BRAS KYI 'BREL PA 'THAD TSUL JI LTAR YIN ZHE NA,
wylie: gnyis pa ni, dngos po rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par 'dod pa'i phyogs la, kun gzhi sogs khas ma blangs kyang las 'bras kyi 'brel pa 'thad tshul ji ltar yin zhe na
english: Here is the second point [of still another discussion]. One may ask the following: Those who believe that entities have no natural existence [meaning the Madhyamika Prasangika (or Consequence) School] do not accept the concepts of a foundation consciousness and the like; how then is it that they can still assert that all the workings of karma and its consequences are totally right and proper?

acip: ,NYON MONGS 'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS STONG BZHIN DU RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR SNANG BA SGYU MA DANG 'DRA BA DE'I DUS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAS RTZA BA NAS SPONG MI NUS SNYAM DU SNYING LA 'JIGS PA SPONG LA STONG NYID RTOGS PA'I SHES RAB BSKYED NAS NYON MONGS SPANG BA'I PHYIR BRTZON PA BSTEN PAR RIGS KYI DE LTAR NUS BZHIN DU DON MED PA NYID DU BDAG LA DMYAL BA LA SOGS PA'I NGAN SONG RNAMS SU CI STE GNOD PA BYED DU 'JUG STE 'JUG PAR MI RIGS SO, , SNGA MA RNAMS SA BON PHYUNG NA GNAS DE DAG TU MI GNAS PA LA YANG BSHAD DO,
wylie: nyon mongs 'di ni rang bzhin gyis grub pas stong bzhin du rang bzhin gyis grub par snang ba sgyu ma dang 'dra ba de'i dus rang bzhin gyis grub pas rtsa ba nas spong mi nus snyam du snying la 'jigs pa spong la stong nyid rtogs pa'i shes rab bskyed nas nyon mongs spang ba'i phyir brtson pa bsten par rigs kyi de ltar nus bzhin du don med pa nyid du bdag la dmyal ba la sogs pa'i ngan song rnams su ci ste gnod pa byed du 'jug ste 'jug par mi rigs so, , snga ma rnams sa bon phyung na gnas de dag tu mi gnas pa la yang bshad do
english: One might have the following thought: "These mental afflictions are empty of any natural kind of existence, but at the same time they do appear to have natural existence, and so they are like an illusion. As long as this is the case--because they do exist through some nature of their own--I could never eliminate them from their root." It is good though if I can eliminate this fear from my heart, and rely on the practice of making great efforts to remove my mental afflictions, through working to develop the wisdom which perceives emptiness. Given that I therefore have at the present moment the ability to remove these afflictions, it is not good on the other hand that I subject myself pointlessly to the sufferings of the lower realms, to hells and the rest. Why should I put myself through these pains? Some commentators have also explained the previous lines as referring to the fact that, once we remove the seeds for the mental afflictions, they can no longer stay in these various places.

acip: MDOR NA ZHI GNAS LA BRTEN NAS GNAS LUGS KYI DON BSGOM PAR BYA STE DE YANG NGA'I SNYAM PA'I NGA NI PHUNG PO LA BTAGS PA TZAM DU BZHAG PAR ZAD KYIS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA DANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DANG , RANG DBANG BA'I SDOD LUGS SU GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAS GANG ZAG GI YOD PA NI MING GI THA SNYAD KYIS BZHAG PA TZAM DANG , BTAGS NAS YOD PA DANG LTOS PA'I TSUL GYIS YOD PA KHO NAR ZAD PAS RANG BZHIN MED DO SNYAM DU YID LA BYA'O, , DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO LA SOGS PA'I CHOS THAMS CAD LA SBYAR NAS BSGOM PAR BYA'O,
wylie: mdor na zhi gnas la brten nas gnas lugs kyi don bsgom par bya ste de yang nga'i snyam pa'i nga ni phung po la btags pa tsam du bzhag par zad kyis rang bzhin gyis grub pa dang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa dang , rang dbang ba'i sdod lugs su grub pa cung zad kyang med pas gang zag gi yod pa ni ming gi tha snyad kyis bzhag pa tsam dang , btags nas yod pa dang ltos pa'i tshul gyis yod pa kho nar zad pas rang bzhin med do snyam du yid la bya'o, , de bzhin du phung po la sogs pa'i chos thams cad la sbyar nas bsgom par bya'o
english: To summarize, we must undertake to meditate upon the real nature of things, basing this analysis upon the practice of meditative quietude. The "me" you think of when you say "it's mine" is nothing more than a projection that you lay on the heaps or parts that make you up. It has not the slightest bit of any natural existence, of any definitive existence, of any independent way of being. The existence of a person is something which happens only by virtue of an idea; the person exists only through projections, only in dependence on other things, and nothing more. Practice thinking of things this way: see that they have no nature of their own. Continue in your meditation, applying this same concept to every existing object: to the parts of a person, and everything else as well. Contemplation Thirty-Seven Pray They All Be Bodhisattvas (The following contemplations are all from the "Chapter on Dedication")

english: One may begin with the following question: Just how is it—in the case of those who assert that there is nothing at all which exists through any nature of its own—that we can we can say that the connection between karma and its consequences is all perfectly acceptable, even without accepting concepts such as foundation consciousness?

acip: MI MKHAS PA GANG DAG GIS NI SNANG TZAM GYIS 'DUS BYAS LA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS SKYE BA DANG 'JIG PA RNAM PAR BRTAGS PA DE DAG GIS NI RTEN CING 'BREL PAR 'BYUNG BA THOG MA DANG DBUS DANG THA MA DANG BRAL BA 'KHOR LO LTA BU'I 'GRO BA STE 'JUG TSUL RNAM PAR MI SHES SHING MI RTOGS TE, RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA LA SKYE BA DANG 'JIG PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR,
wylie: mi mkhas pa gang dag gis ni snang tsam gyis 'dus byas la rang gi mtshan nyid kyis skye ba dang 'jig pa rnam par brtags pa de dag gis ni rten cing 'brel par 'byung ba thog ma dang dbus dang tha ma dang bral ba 'khor lo lta bu'i 'gro ba ste 'jug tshul rnam par mi shes shing mi rtogs te, rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa la skye ba dang 'jig pa mi srid pa'i phyir
english: Those who have no nature of being wise imagine-simply because of the way things appear-that produced things have a starting and an ending, through some definition of their own. People like this have no understanding at all of the workings of all those entities which occur in a dependent relationship: of how they operate. They cannot grasp how much like a wheel these things are, devoid of any kind of starting point, or middle point, or ending point. And all this because they cannot see how-with things that exist in & of themselves-the very events of starting & stopping are impossible. The two realities, defined
